request: Improve hierarchy and design of compact browser chrome
title: Align browser chrome visual hierarchy
purpose: Align address bar and content and reduce competing sidebar emphasis

files.purpose: Align address bar and content and reduce competing sidebar emphasis
files.previous_behavior: Address bar started left of the content edge, stopped at a fixed maximum width and competed with the tinted new-tab button.
files.new_behavior: Navigation occupies the sidebar-width region; address field aligns with content and expands to available width. New-tab action is neutral, top icons have consistent dimensions and window controls use restrained contrast.
files.data_impact: none: CSS-only visual adjustments without persistence changes.
files.access_control_impact: none: control behavior and permissions unchanged.
risks: Collapsed sidebar keeps the top navigation width fixed to retain all navigation buttons.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild; point the desktop shortcut to the previous executable. No stored data changes.

production_safety.operational_data: No operational profiles or settings were read or modified. Headless tests used synthetic content.
external_side_effects: Local native/publish-refined build and desktop shortcut update; active Oinzi remains untouched.

verification.evidence: Headless browser: address/content edges align within 1px at 780 and 1380px, no horizontal overflow, no page errors; settings isolation, drag placement and compact header regressions pass. Rendered screenshot visually reviewed.

verification.command: dotnet publish native/native.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o native/publish-refined -p:NoWarn=MSB3277 -v quiet

residual_risks: Native desktop rendering at non-default DPI and live website combinations were not manually exercised.
